t: The word imperialism took its present sense in English in the late 1870s, but the extension of power over foreign nations is as old as history; its most intense modern phase, the Age of Imperialism, is commonly said to have ended in 1914.

Its advocates justified it as a civilizing mission backed by theories of race, while imperial rule brought atrocities such as those of the Congo Free State, the Herero and Namaqua genocide and the ethnic cleansing of the Circassians.
Hobson and Lenin explained imperialism as a product of capitalism; after World War II, movements in the colonies, Pan-Africanism among them, won independence and ended most of the European empires.
dyk: Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905 shook the world: never before had an Asian nation defeated a European power, and it became an example for Asian countries in the fight against the Western powers for decolonization.
ev: France seizes Algiers, beginning its second colonial empire
The term imperialism is applied to the British Empire, introduced in its present sense by opponents of Benjamin Disraeli
John A. Hobson publishes Imperialism: A Study, arguing that empire drained money needed at home
After scandal upon scandal over atrocities in the Congo Free State, Belgium is forced to take it over from King Leopold II
Lenin’s Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism portrays imperialism as monopoly capitalism on a world scale
India becomes independent, with partition, as decolonization movements arise across the British Empire
France grants Algeria independence, ending most of its second colonial empire
Edward Said’s Orientalism describes Western knowledge of the East as a justification of empire

f.thinkers: its advocates Joseph Chamberlain, Cecil Rhodes, Jules Ferry, Lord Cromer, Lord Curzon, Lord Milner and the writer Rudyard Kipling; the political geographers Friedrich Ratzel and Halford Mackinder; its theorists and critics John A. Hobson, Vladimir Lenin, Joseph Schumpeter, Walter Rodney and Edward Said
f.texts: John A. Hobson, Imperialism: A Study (1902); Vladimir Lenin, Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism (1916); Rosa Luxemburg, The Accumulation of Capital; Walter Rodney, How Europe Underdeveloped Africa (1972); Edward Said, Orientalism (1978)
f.ideas: extending a state’s power over foreign nations by conquest, rule and influence; a civilizing mission and the White Man’s Burden; racial hierarchy, given a supposedly scientific basis by Social Darwinism; environmental determinism, which cast tropical peoples as in need of European guidance; colonies as sources of raw materials and captive markets; empire “informally if possible and formally if necessary”
f.today: the term is often used in international propaganda as a pejorative for expansionist foreign policy; Russia under Vladimir Putin has been described as neo-imperialist since the 2010s and is accused of neo-colonialism in Africa; neocolonialism and cultural imperialism remain subjects of debate
